tool.name: DiameterJ fiber diameter
tool.description: measure fiber diameters from a segmented image

param.name: foreground
param.label: Fiber foreground color
param.help: DiameterJ requires a segmented binary image. Select the color representing fibers.

param.name: orientation_radius
param.label: Orientation neighborhood radius (pixels)
param.help: Local fiber direction is estimated by principal-component analysis of skeleton pixels in this radius.

param.name: minimum_mesh_area
param.label: Minimum mesh-hole area (pixels squared)
param.help: DiameterJ's original Analyze Particles workflow excludes pores smaller than 10 pixels squared.

tool.help:
**What it does**
DiameterJ measures fiber diameters in a segmented two-dimensional image. This headless implementation follows DiameterJ's central diameter-distribution method: it skeletonizes the fiber mask, calculates a Euclidean distance map, and samples twice the local distance-to-background along the fiber centerline.
The tool produces diameter statistics and plots, mesh-hole areas, a mesh-hole histogram and porosity, a local fiber-orientation distribution and plot, the distance map, and sensitive and Voronoi centerlines. The diameter plot shows frequency against fiber diameter as a filled black distribution and labels its modal diameter. Mesh holes touching an image edge are excluded, matching DiameterJ's particle-analysis convention. Orientation is reported from 0 to 180 degrees and estimated from local skeleton neighborhoods.
Fiber intersections are clustered and classified as three- or four-branch junctions. Radius samples near these junctions are removed from the diameter distribution. The summary reports fiber area, weighted centerline lengths, intersection density, characteristic length, and an iterative super-pixel diameter. The diagnostic TIFF shows the sensitive centerline in red, excluded intersection regions in yellow, and junction centers in cyan. These headless measurements reproduce the documented DiameterJ workflow but may differ numerically from the historical interactive macro and OrientationJ implementation.
Inputs should already be segmented, with fibers represented by one binary color. Non-binary inputs are automatically thresholded with ImageJ's Default method.
All measurements are in pixels unless a physical pixel size and unit are supplied. The histogram bin width is specified in pixels and is converted using the same pixel size.
DiameterJ is most accurate when fibers are at least 10 pixels wide and less than 10% of the image's smallest dimension. Fiber diameters greater than 512 pixels are outside the validated range of the original software.
The summary includes a **DiameterJ suitability** status and the percentage of centerline samples inside the validated diameter interval. Apply this tool to a Galaxy dataset collection to screen an EM zoom series image by image; Galaxy preserves one set of outputs per input image.
**References**
- `NIST DiameterJ <https://www.nist.gov/mml/bbd/biomaterials/diameterj>`_ - `ImageJ DiameterJ documentation <https://imagej.net/plugins/diameterj>`_
